The new Diarrhea Planet is one that is trying harder to get you to understand their Diarrhea ethos, and it works - especially on the amazing, soaring, splattering album closer.
If you believe you don't have time for 16 minutes and 5 seconds of poppy punk joy, you are not living.
Meaty, mid-range rock bolstered by troll-sounding men and topped with Polly Jean's wise, knowing cadence.
Who's looking to get down to super deep global awareness protest rock?
Harvey abstains from introspection and instead uses her gifted lyrical abilities to set scenes and describe harsh places and hard moments amid soundscapes that are organic, propelling, and genuine.
I can't decide if it's track 3 or 4 that's the hero of this weird little album, but I think it's probably 3.
This best new band contender that flexes a ton of sonic variety is at their best when they are shoegazing left of the dial .

Nels Cline saves you a trip to the used record bin with this old-timey album that feels romantic, warm, and retro, but prepare for a handful of forward-thinking moments that remind you that the maestro is in control.

If the world woke up tomorrow not realizing KAYTRANADA or his music ever existed (kinda like what happens in that Beatles movie), a DJ could simply hit play on this album and fill a portion of their set with boogie wonders and people would likely proclaim them as their new favorite local DJ.
Hip-hop based dance beats featuring some of my groove loving favorites (Craig David, Aluna George, Vic Mensa, BadBadNotGood, Phonte, Anderson Paak, Little Dragon)… this album was made for me.
Soft indie gem layered with tension of uncertainty, opportunity and aspiration that feels familiar but new.
In the Cistern, every needle has a destiny.
Expensive organic cheese puff shows some nice textural contrast upon approach
The quality of feeling in an old man's voice, laced in harmony with angelic country music goddesses, is impossible to turn your shoulder from.
These duets are perfect and they're a great chapter in the book of Prine, and as a fan of his, it's interesting (dare I say sad) to hear his voice become more fragile, old, and tender.
Jaar gives us a masterclass in tension vs calm, chaos vs serenity, and found sound vs instrumentation in this sprawling, spacey, emotional LP that is amazingly impactful on a proper hifi.
the balance of ambience and groove creates an escape into an ultimate levitation of cool

At first listen, I felt like 22, A Million was Justin Vernon making music for the music's sake instead of the author or listener's sake, but diving more deeply into this distorted galaxy of songs, I find some of the key Bon Iver elements and emotional weightiness as found on For Emma and Bov Iver , however clouded with effects, and they are very rewarding.
It left me feeling cold: nothing offensive, nothing new, something to arouse you.
This shit is straight free jazz and now the kingpin in my argument that we're living in the greatest R&B moment since the 90s.
A tight proggy journey always makes me feel like the world is a substantial amount more orderly than I usually think it is.
Lots of talent behind these tracks that are intricately layered cakes of sound and structure that consequently are able to engage and sweetly surprise even after repeated listens.
Sting meets fun. the band and whisper-sings embarrassingly unsubtle words to embarrassingly unsubtle melodies that will make you feel embarrassed.
A capable group of musicians who should take more risks lyrically and sonically and in doing so would create something more memorable and less fluffy.

This polarizing album had me feeling love, hate, and everything in between with its mish-mashing of styles and sounds, and in the end, I was appreciative that for having in my life (if not a bit uncomfortable)
Early Foo Fighters (best Foo Fighters) meets classic blues rock to put you in the mood of summer.
For better or worse, Benjamin's lyrics and vocal performance didn't grab me, but I found myself completely in love with the multitude of amazing guitar tones this axe man brought to the table
A parade through a sandwich shop on a sad political afternoon.
Jim James has the uncanny ability to make music that passes all the tests (fundamentally sound, inspired, skillful) that I just don't like, but the covers on this album are definitely for someone .

Remember the scene in Wayne's World where Wayne sees Cassandra at her warehouse show for the first time and he's hovering toward her but Stacy keeps getting in his way? It was like that, but the warehouse was a smokey 70s pillow pad, Cassandra was a solid instrumental groove and Stacy was Jim James whisper singing patronizing cliche life lessons.
I chose this album craving the female driven folksy alt rock Vagabon gave us in Infinite Worlds to find an autumn rainy day electronic evolution that delivered more value with every listen.

Wierdo prog R&B with guests like Kendrick, Pharrell and Flying Lotus is like when you realize your neighbor is a unicorn.
It's ("Jamiroquai") the band, not the man.
A neo-disco gem in which Jamiroquai never takes the spotlight off the ball, never wants your foot to stop tapping for more than a few seconds.
There's so much talent, I only wish the songs made sense.
As a Melvins and Mars Volta fan, I found myself more distracted - trying to pick out the players and parts - than enjoying this angular yet steady album of songs that are just ok.
A harsh collage of whipping and sludgy proggy rock smartly and intricately delivered and like a liquor that burns the throat, cannot be easily consumed in large quantities.
hmmm… HMMMmmmm… bitch went tribal… YES
Summer emotion & party album of the year 2017.
Ms. Gonzalez has crafted a perfect assemblage of songs that will take you down memory road with silky R&B sounds while keeping you in the present with huge production and savvy lyrical content.
Somewhat technical rock, abrasive, hard to listen to, smacking of Pleasure Club but without the catch, but 'Providence' stands out as an instance of the group's having found itself.
There are trinkets here and there with the guitar work that piqued my listening ears, but I was left unimpressed with songsmanship and a bit worn out by this stuff.
A wonderful kind of spoken-word-over-ambient-music thing with occasional snippets of melody and lyrics that you'll like if you're into that sort of thing and that is pleasant even if you're not.
A nice companion to Forgiveness Rock Record , BSC stays in their lane for the most part and delivers what I call Collective Rock for the indie masses.

As the evolution of Broken Social Scene veers away from the aural adventure of You Forgot It In People to the epic energetic soundscape kicked off by It's All Gonna Break on their self titled sophomore, it's departs from broad supergroup sound that I loved.
It's off-season transiberian orchestra material - I'm sure of it.

After about 15 minutes of this album a number of different soundscapes and genres have been covered and it's clear there's a significant order of magnitude (oceansize) being the goal which doesn't make for an effortless listen but if you're willing to stand on deck and hold on through the waves and sprays it's ultimately rewarding and impressive.

Home recording among friends at its finest, Cerulean explores a vast landscape of 90s- and 00s-inspired styles ranging from My Morning Jacket to Sunny Day Real Estate to Bright Eyes to Weezer, among other generation-defining white dude rock and alternative music.

Even though from moment to moment I find much of Brutalism hard to listen to, I believe that the point is bigger than any moment and worthy of opening up to, and on top of that there are many awesome rock moments and Lock, Stock, and Two Smoking Barrels-esque swagger-lyrics.
Brutalism is a Sex Pistols inspired, much needed shot in the arm to a year who's best music thus far is of the more gentle variety.

In the trifecta of perfect punk—humor, hooks and brooding—IDLES debut album, Brutalism, felt more humor first where as Joy as an Act of Resistance feels more brooding first, therefore I feel like the titles of their two albums should be switched.
Pretty awesome jangly and peppy pissed off rock from guys that don't give a fuck and would think I'm a tool.

Oh baby, you're in for LCD + better if you can look past the cliched non-retire leading to a less snark more feeling album (but not goodbye to all snark, e.g., "these morning ablutions are just part of the dance").

An album that mashes the sounds of Modest Mouse and the Yeah Yeah Yeahs, with a slightly dark and mournful tinge and otherwise sunny, guitar driven sounds that's eclectic enough to keep the listener's ear perked up throughout.
As much as i enjoyed this album, wolf parade suffers from awesome debut disease for me where i expect every song to hit me with a fresh sound and lyrical hooks that speak to my soul.
Fans of Fever and The Knife will get what they want from this moody, alien-voiced artist on an album that doesn't reach new ground for her, but stays rightly in her unique lane.
The highs of The New Monday are very high—jazzy, dashy-smooth grooves—though many songs lack intuitable structure.
A soupy mix of heritage house and REMIXERS BEWARE Ice Breaker is already perfect so don't even bother.

An album that I'd choose for default music for my inner speaker that balances the best of classic groove based jazzy house and brings it to today (or you know maybe 20 years ago) with perfect drops of left field hip-hop.
almost 1
I won't be returning to this gentle, brooding, jazzy nonsense on my own, but if I am at a party where hard drugs are involved, I will be the one sneaking it onto the high-fi.
The soundtrack of the opiate crisis.
Never does the sun shine on The OOZ, but it's seedy back alley darkness and filth can be mesmerizing and Krule folds words together to make goblin origami.
Welcome to Planet Earth, where you will find lush green landscapes, beautiful deep blue oceans, and barely the need for one Vampire Weekend.

Music made to appeal to "the youth" and music made by them are two distinguishable groups, and Hippo Campus's first full act hopefully sets the stage for a progressively ambitious and varied future catalog and I'd be remiss not to add that their torch has some of Vampire Weekend's flame burning within it.
If you need a change in the world, listen to Kaitlyn Aurelia Smith.
Filled with movement, kinetic sounds and noises, that brought me to a version of alice, through the looking glass.
Full of richly creative and enjoyably peculiar sounds and sequences, the album flirts with emitting sharpened and formed songs and musical ideas more often than it delivers them.

Daytime in electronic disco village is short, making dusk a time of anticipatory chill before the real boogie begins.
As though there was some music blood type, Parcels pulses with me in a special way.
A sequence of medium-sized notes that make medium-feeling melodies in a wonderfully consistent way (all melody?).
All Melody delivers to my expectation of contemporary classical music, pushing sound, taking influence from vast genres while remaining melodic, engaging and inclusive.

There is such a precious quality to the malaise of Yo La Tengo, and this album, which speaks to the terrible situation we humans find ourselves in, lays bare their truly unique way of writing about such painful truths in such beautiful ways.
I hope Yo La Tengo's pace of continually releasing new music that feels like a fresh perspective on the same soft noise melodic magic inspires the kids to start shoegazing right.
By turns utterly dumb and annoyingly brash, this album is one to be forgotten.

A mushy layer cake of inspirations, young fathers is a TV on the Radio base with a layer of blood orange, a thin layer of Sampha and over sweetened with epic indie pop frosting and artificial west coast hip hop and r&b sprinkles… I'm not a fan of mushy cake, but it sounds kinda good.

Ought have come a long way since their very punkish debut, with the band now treading in more eclectic and worldly territory, and Room Inside the World just might make the UK Loving, Mark E Smith Loving, Rainy Day Serious-Face friend in your life (or you) feel like they like to feel.
My high, high hopes resulting from track 1 were not quite borne out by the rest of the record, but Con Todo El Mundo is super cool, like Ratatat with slower and groovier edges.
How do I visit this Persian Disco Palace?
Liquid, summer, sex.

Dirty Computer is not only a lush landscape of pop goodness and rhymes that confirm Janelle Monet as a bad bitch to be reckoned with, but as a bonus this gem of an album provides the world's first definitive confirmation of the afterlife, being that it was indisputably co-written and executive produced by Prince - He is risen! 10s 10s 10s.
candy apple sings like a cherub amidst drastic changes in production

Kacey completes her trifecta of amazing albums (not including the wonderful christmas lp) with a spellbinding set of tunes that highlights her ability to lace traditional country with modern witticisms and sounds, highlighted by Space Cowboy, which is the greatest ballad in at least the last decade.
These undefiably simple, precious and timeless love tunes bridge genres through the mastery and magic of soft rock.
As in other records, her nonchalant vocal dispensations flutter above the cool swagger of the "90s-hip" rock band she leads.
In a brief but meaningful milestone, Courtney Barnett adds little more sound and a sprinkle of grunge and continues to extend her reign as one of today's best singer songwriters.
Forgettable bedroom stuff that's cool for a teenager with a computer.

After like 5 full listens, while I know there is a place in my musical frequency to enjoy thoughtful emo girl pop, I think I just need to accept that I currently don't have the frequency to actually hear this album.

Disappointing: I really wanted to like rejjie's little girlfriend, but the only parts I liked were production on songs that sounded like Dear Annie b-sides, and no matter how ironically they were written, the dumb girl lyrics were trash.
Project Pablo delights the listener with tunes that sound really familiar to any DJ who soaked up a bunch of stuff on Seasons, Guidance, etc back in the day.
This sensible summery house will work great on your yacht (or shantyboat ), though it may provide a little too much bounce for your dentist's chair

Regardless of whether I want to or not, I listen to Drake, and I generally like listening to Drake as long as I don't have to hear Drake, and there will never be a need for me to think anymore about it.
In my opinion there's no envelope pushing lyrically or musically and the result is both underwhelming and akin to trying to eat cotton candy for breakfast, lunch, and dinner.
Relaxed vocals, retro grooves that give credit to their predecessors, a motley set of instruments digital and otherwise — Hive Mind is the album of mid summer.
its a great time for quality r&b, and hive mind, with its summer guitary, bbq vibe just might take the cake this year.
Add The Internet to the list of solid west coasters pushing r&b and hip-hop to new happy place with a jazz influenced vibe.
Previous chart success and a target audience and fan base that seem nebulous reflexively invoke suspicion in me but damn I really dig a lot of the textures, beats, and creativity behind this album.
Maybe this entire album is ironic, i don't know, but regardless I am offended by the name of the band, the album, and the off-key singing.
Moments of glory washed in a sea of monotony; it's an interesting sea but oh so vast.

(Hi, Frank Ocean!) ASTROWORLD is much like ingesting and enjoying an edible in the back of your friend's car during nighttime as an adolescent: medium risk, physically enjoyable, engaging with your heart rate
Do the kids spend all their time watching porn on heroine these days, cuz sex and drugs has never sounded more oozy.
Blissful, soft and new, like a bright fall day in bed after you first hooked up with your soulmate.
Sparse yet rich, confident yet vulnerable, the album doesn't force sound or rush pace setting a beautiful table on which to dine.
Mitski weaves between genres and vibes but there is always that singular, unique voice guiding songs that stand up as perhaps the year's best.
Wow she's cool and that's a solid album.

If you ever find yourself on Mars atop Olympus Mons (a mountain twice the height of Everest) and you notice a gigantic huge dust storm approaching that might result in your disintegration listen to this album, or if you're on Earth taking a walk, or sitting on your couch, or anywhere.

No track on this sprawling, beautiful set of tunes better exemplifies just how much Deafheaven has expanded their reach (metal, emo, classic rock), and how much George Clarke's vocals are being treated as an instrumental layer than Honeycomb - one of the year's best songs thus far.
Breaking News: demon spawn piglet abducts superbly talented rock band and forces them to record.

KV delivers.
Exactly half the album is a stretch forward, while the other half is comfortable KV listening using chords and sounds that aren't quite exhausted yet.
gimme some of this euro house pop all day, i love it so, and if i chose another, it'd be kylie minogue.
Robyn brings back dancefloor inspiration from the decade of her debut for those who are needing to dance to forget

I am here for this slightly more understated version of Robyn in a soundtrack to a late 80s/early 90s teen slasher film with a happy ending (as evidenced by the last track, "Ever Again," which is the CUT).
Watching the Anima short on Netflix was somehow less confusing than this album, which I look forward to confusing me more and more.
Surprise surprise: I love a lush Thom Yorke soundscape that's perfect for long drives at dusk in places you don't belong.
There's a few moments here that harken back to a simpler, more pure time, and to be honest, I live for those moments.

A chameleon diva is a rare creature that makes good pop that always feels relevant, authentic and comfortable. (Sidenote - I revisited Mariah's self titled debut album that I loved in 1990 as a 7th grader and it's the same model… RnB was so pure back then).
Neo blues mixed with James Blake-inspired soul, covered in syrup, served at room temperature.
This is a fine album that twists contemporary radio friendly soulful roots rock with reggae and will leave hozier drooling.

Good singer, sounds like he’s stuffed up but not even as a bad thing, and the album is in a lane that feels safe, yearning to trend, like a really good Instagram pic of a latte in a hip coffee shop with a cool filter.
The Resplendent Quetzal. striking in her looks and song as ever, commands attention and a platform for her beauty, but alas, the Quetzal only knows one song.

I revisited Beirut's debut (an album that i love) in preparation for this, and while I miss the raw euro street sound of Gulag Orkestar, I appreciate and enjoy the Beirut sound on a larger more refined soundscape.
The leisurely and gently paced jams are warming and well crafted, so much so that it might be an ideal soundtrack candidate for some of the world's best light napping.
I love how it sounds (like an extended summer road trip when you like somebody and the attraction is high) but for me there's nothing memorable when it's over.
This shit is straight free jazz and now the kingpin in my argument that we're living in the greatest R&B moment since the 90s.

An album worth investing in (it took me 10 voluntary listens to finally love it), Solange's collection of R'n'B textures and melodic repition to create an approachable experimental soulful levitation session was a pleasantly surprising celebration.
Says so much with so little, paints with my memories, tickles something that hasn't been touched since Carrie and Lowell.
It shines with an honest vibrancy that cannot be forced, and I could not have imagined it before I heard it.
I couldn't break seeing transitional montage of serious Will Ferrell either being broken hearted or on the comeback but always looking confused.
A modern adult contemporary ode to settling, to being lulled by the surge of emotions you mistook for love that ultimately left you drunk on powerlessness.

Yung's tunes sound as if they were born from Play-Doh, and mushed through various machines labelled, "Swim up pool bar, spring break", "Rolling with the homies LOL", "Smoking weed for the first time, OMG", etc.
I appreciate Billie's smooth transition onto the sexy sophomore album phase of her career track, while maintaining her authenticity and highlighting her fantastic voice.
Damn, even the guitars and mics sound like a different era, to say nothing of the exceptional vocals on this amazing mix of tunes that'll get your soul wet with feelings.
If TheBolg worked on a scale of new sweet sweet soul to brighten a lazy Sunday morning, this would be a 10.

With the instrumental and vocal (lead and backup) tools and chops to faithfully reconstruct a rich 60s/70s R&B sound Durand and his band do just that while the only boundaries they push are the boundaries of time.
A twee dagger to the gut of the Harvey W club.

TTC is still forcing the listener to get over his self-importance, but Flower Boy is his most complete offering yet, and the singing guests and the eclectic production make it cohesive with most of today's top-tier hip hop.

Maturing from a brash provocateur to someone whose horizons have clearly expanded, the album makes me want to be in the back seat of a car staring out the window listening while impossibly trying to notice and process everything and everyone I’m seeing.
I liked it - multilayered, stimulating, solid break-up album.
Riding through neon streets in LA at night, bobbing your head, almost as if you are a character in GTA (props to the album cover for portraying the sounds in a fun way).
I went from driving a ferrari at night in Miami the 80s to playing Out Run which was a regression

Dreamy and poppily layered but not to the point where I just think about cotton candy, I think about humans holding and eating that cotton candy, flawed, sugary, occasionally gyrating.
I hear the hooks and get the appeal, but it would take a lot of radio play that I will never have before I start biting this uber mush of international pop.

Even though my brother has been sneaking kpop into my psyche for years, it's still deliciously disorienting to hear poppy hip hop in a language I don't understand - super fun album that just makes me feel good.
This album is like a flitting wren delicately whispering into my ear, tickling the little hairs of my body, but then I just it want it to stop cuz it's like a BIRD flying right by my head!
Bedroom pop refined enough to please an audiophile with songs that tug at strings you didn't know you had.
I have to say, amid the excellent cast in retro prog space jazz you expect from flying lotus, the middle section between titties in the face and the creepy tommy fire story really stands out.
It's the live feed from last 3 day outdoor festival into the apocalypse - dance through all the love and rage and fears you ever had.

I never felt at ease especially during that first listen because at any moment a song spin in any direction including pulverizing sound but on occasion it feels exciting to be like Lieutenant Dan up on top of the mast in the middle of the nasty storm, embracing it, and after it's passed you just think - whoa.

We get the full KDJ spectrum on this one, and you can listen to it alongside Silentintroduction without feeling like time has passed: the man remains the cream of the crop in house music and we're so lucky to have him.
Moodyman's love for Prince was my inspiration for choosing this album and the presence of The Purple One is clearly sprinkled in subtly in vocals and beats throughout this lovely layered house gem.

(more!) Bedroom pop in 2019 from Clairo - a young, fresh songwriting talent that takes you through the issues surrounding relationships, mental health, and wanting with a wisdom that is well beyond her years.

T.Swift gives us hints of her best style with the heart-warming love songs, but remains distracted by more modern attempts at rebel pop that render the album inconsistent and begs the question….does she need to calm down?

Team TayTay's ability to make journal entries into perfect stadium pop is masterful and while there is some evolution of sound in a few tracks here, I feel like it's a lot of the same Taylorisms that have a surplus in my life.

As the cover would suggest, Beck comes through with a half-hearted Japanese AOR effort that falls short in just about every way, but there are a few crumbles of good Beck - be it rhythm guitar sounds or vocal melodies - that give the album just enough oomph for die-hard Beck fans to keep it on the shelf.

Their fuzzy low-fi songs are built up around snazzy little recurring riffs and licks and I'd enjoy seeing them in an unfinished basement at a house party and if I were lucky they'd pour a beer on my head as they sang about a medieval wall.

Big Thief dominated 2019 with two amazing albums, the better of which is this, the ever-curious-yet-familiar, not-sad-but-not-happy, dream-like folk collection that catapults them into best-band-of-our-era territory.

I thought perhaps my embrace of talk radio meant that I was maturing and I might be a fan of new adult contemporary music, but apparently I only love old adult contemporary music… maybe if I'm forced to listen to this on the radio for the next decade, I'll like it in 20 years.

If the world woke up tomorrow not realizing KAYTRANADA or his music ever existed (kinda like what happens in that Beatles movie), a DJ could simply hit play on this album and fill a portion of their set with boogie wonders and people would likely proclaim them as their new favorite local DJ.
Hip-hop based dance beats featuring some of my groove loving favorites (Craig David, Aluna George, Vic Mensa, BadBadNotGood, Phonte, Anderson Paak, Little Dragon)… this album was made for me.

The Kaputt days are gone, and Have We Met sees Dan Bejar sifting through some of the UK-inspired darkness dripping from Ken, then wrapping it up in protofunk elegies meant for the modern grave-digging renaissance music lover.

It definitely sounds like Tame Impala with a few quirky changes in direction and it definitely is high quality music, but lacks that certain something that will make me put it on more as the year goes on.
I believe that the groove, melodies and feels are all in there, so I'm sure my rating will increase through the year as the mush of Tame Impala reveals itself in definitive moments
Fiona's new record is inventive, engaging, and prone to keeping you on your toes: not unlike the boardgame Tzolk'in, which does the same with unique game parts and play.
Like a wild contraption of a vehicle that lumbers and lurches full of clicking and clanking and puffs of smoke it is obtuse and difficult to manage and miraculously unique.

There's a sparseness to the album though it feels anything but bare rather it leaves space between it's shapes and lets them dance with and respond to one another though it can feel a bit like sketches and not fully formed works.
I initially resisted being taken in by this super pleasant collection of electro-pop singles that grow from isolation to celebration to bliss, and then i submitted and now i think i'm dead.

Things I loved about this album were OPN's production, the slow jams, and funny enough JC's job as DJ throughout the set, and though the heaters felt a bit stale, The Weeknd nevertheless added a worthy entry to his impressive resume.
My favorite part of this album is the soft rock radio station concept and I dunno, it's cool I guess, and I'm sure I'll like it more once it's tapeworm it's way into my subconscious

Aside from the simply gorgeous production on this album I have 2 theories - it's unrelatable fuckboy content with an out of place totally PG 3-song arc of 80s short film perfection beginning with Blinding Lights - OR - everything about this is 100% intentional start to finish in a nuanced character study of the complexity of what created and drives said fuckboy (broken heart, drug problem, and any number of DSM-5 diagnoses) who I still don't feel sorry for.
Chip Wickham's Blue and Red gives me hope that there is a magical flute in a tropical space spa in a hidden dungeon somewhere in the original Legend of Zelda for NES

I love R&B slow jams, not usually in album form… and usually soft… and flowing… not hard and conflicted
This late-career collection is vibrant, colorful, and worldly without losing any of the emotional weight I rightfully expect from the legend herself.

Check your respectability politics and fear of the word pussy at the door, then come on in and shake your ass, get some money, and curse somebody the fuck out (this party slaps!).

Considering live music is not a thing right now, this recording made it easy for me to picture these musicians surrounding me; unsure of whether listening to a live album would lead to pleasure or torture, I came out feeling like I had experienced something that was well worth the focus.
Consider this a soundtrack to some daily activity that plays nicely in the background with simple beats and sounds that wash in and out of your mind with little thought needed.
There are segments which create enjoyable chill but driving musical spaces but what are intended to be the climactic and impactful segments tend to be where it falls out of favor for me.

I've always found the path for contemporary soft rock americana to find my heart is via singles on young adult dramas—for example, Arlo McKinley has a better chance resonating with me served during a controversial wedding double episode of Felicity.
In a time when I'm constantly defaulting to comfort music but craving new music, I was so happy to be listening to a weird fun groovy 90s swedish indie throwback that is new to my ears.

Even though I don't love every single track, from the time I first heard it back in 1996 this is a near perfect album for my particular love of unexpected rhythms, nostalgic fun, and a fascinating voice that pulls/lulls it all together.
As the kids say, this album is a Whole Ass Vibe, and more than it is just a collection of songs about having sex with animals, it is the birth of what I hope to be a prominent genre: New Age Rap.
The rhymes delivered with silky cool swagger and often at a volume you'd talk at if you weren't trying to wake someone up are featured and set over gentle synthy beats.

In 1993, The Flaming Lips (opening for Candlebox at the Aragon Ballroom) was the first live music experience without my parents that I ever had and because of that they are locked into the like category even as they drift farther into a drug dream saga that rides the line between bliss and paranoia—having Kacey Musgraves float in and out of your drug dreams always helps.
the best part of the relatively uneventful unambitious but kinda pretty camping trip was when Brian suggested maybe it's all a conspiracy theory… and now that i think about it… maybe it was!

The album basks you in calm, sunny, and peaceful waters in which schools of harmonious fish bob and weave and a weighted blanket made of guitar strings waits on shore to sooth and comfort as a lazy afternoon ebbs and flows.
Smooth dancehall flows and grooves that probably work better on a tropical beach during sunset, but still work pretty well cooped inside small home office on a nice autumn Minnesotan day.
A mix of fun and seriousness, modern and vintage, with more than a handful of bops, this album makes me nostalgic for the sounds of Lagos.

I needed something new and old to help me look forward and stabilize my turbulence and Jyoti met there and the soundtrack was good, but the it was a little short on guiding groove and a little strong on riding turbulence, so we're still there

Old and wise jams that will slow your heart rate with peaceful keys and arrangements that add just the right about of mellow bite to the perfectly restrained yet careful and enlightened lyrics from someone who I now consider a Master of his work.
Cool and contemporary slo-mo dream spa easy listening.
If the sequel to Willow was a century spanning epic focused on the lives and dramas of the village tavern's family of fiddlers, I think this would be the soundtrack.

soft skipping swifty that breaks for light pop that gets acousticky, which takes a mariachi turn into raggaeton that settles back into light pop that would all likely grow on me if i spend some time with it
It's at its best when it makes me smiley, fingers tapping an uncomplicated beat on the steering wheel, feeling like the sun is shining even if it's not.
The young chef leads with a hint of arrogance, and this is that type of restaurant they warn you about with too many styles of cuisine to master any one, but here I am… asking for seconds.
Last week and this week inspired me to engage in AT40 again and this pop is better than the charts, but I became overwhelmed by the consistency of twee raggaeton.
Confident chill mid temp grooves that get your shoulders bouncing at times with shrill often whisper-sung vocals which I never really warmed to.
There's a flame lit under the album which comes straight from the heart and the fist-pumping vulnerability of tracks like Boomer rules.

Catchy and at times beautiful psych-soul celestial bodies of music glitter as they come in and out of view of foggy intros and outros (many being tracks themselves) that create distance between points in space .
Two Saviors by the Big Thief guitarist is a folk record that makes you wish you were at a cabin drinking coffee, looking out the window at some wood.
Beautiful tender country-cottage front porch sunset with a bunch of artsy city kids napping and chopping vegetables inside.
Like all great vibe records, Who Are You? sounds mystical and cosmic with just the right amount of groove.
Led by the vibraphone, Who Are You? plots a boppy story that journeys from cool to freakout… best for focused listens, not recommended for multitasking with children and house construction.

reviews.text: I appreciate the opportunity of listening to a set of another ones of the best music filled with a variety of affirmation, (mostly self affirmation for the khaled crew, but some sprinkles for me) but the majority of these quality bangers are on the outside of the heavy edge of my banger ranger.
The feel of the whole thing gives me movie montage transitions capturing that "we survived and the best is yet to come" feeling - it's fun!

Catching mist from a neighbor's sprinkler on a hot summer walk yields a measured but potent amount of joy then moments later you're dry and I can listen to this whole album while each time it feels like it took no time at all, was beautiful, and is somewhat nondescript in my memory.

Creative and sincere caricatures of the 70s with a number of solid moments and sounds but when it feels like the tour should be co-billed with The Blue Jean Committee an album will struggle to reach soaring heights.
A fun, raw, soulful tongue-in-cheek romp with the vintage white girl indy darling.
This is a fun, groovy record that is undeniably buoyed by the bops.
Duckwrth defntly brings some postve vibe r&b dance jams, but it's really more of a "I'll reach for the single" type of deal than a "need that albm" situation.

reviews.text: When artists go rock, it can sometimes come across as experimental…this album feels right at home for Willow.
I trust that Willow is sincerely angsty, and I'm sorry that I will she was more jiggy, but I really appreciate being forced to listen to Avril Lavigne
Super fun, and this is definitely her genre, but I can't say that I'll be listening again.
I adore this album's diversity, yet fulfilling cohesion in a world that can sometimes sound like we live in black and white.
I'm not too into ASMR but if I was, I would listen to this album on repeat.
I appreciate Billie's smooth transition onto the sexy sophomore album phase of her career track, while maintaining her authenticity and highlighting her fantastic voice.
An absolutely cosmic collection of groovers that weaves through sunny and shadowy portions of spacetime with a confident strut.
Joyful team psychedelic soul jazz that made me feel like Violet Beauregard on the Wonkatania, but mostly only because she says, "What is this a freakout?"
a solid cillection of r&b that has some rhythmic slapping.
A soft and lovely 25 minute drift with Jorja front loaded with quality low key r&b grooves
As someone who was only familiar with her features on hip hop tracks, it was nice to hear her unique style and exquisite voice on her on terms.
Jose's guitar playing and songwriting have somehow improved and these songs moved me in incredible ways and I DON'T EVEN SPEAK SPANISH!
Jose defies my farty pretensions by making music that's very Jose sounding, but always refreshing and joyfully precious in new ways.
This album is a modern masterpiece that exposes the vulnerabilities of a black, gay man in the hip hop industry. For bop to bop, I have this on heavy rotation.
I was a little hesitant considering the old town road vibe, but this album brings a new perspective to pop stardom and is packed with top 40 hits that I found really likable… and minimally annoying

This sounds like the audio version of the photo dump trend, when he could've taken a page from the Bad Bunny 2020 playbook and released a 12 song album that fucking SLAPPED, surprise B sides a couple months later, and another album to wind out the year - tighten up, J (but I still shook my ass big time).

I absolutely love this mellow R&B album that once in a while will pick the tempo up but overall just slows your heart rate in the most wonderful ways, and maybe what I love most of all….it's about a half-hour long.
There is a cycle in my heart in which a hole grows and it needs to be filled by new neosoul and Wayne Snow has made me whole again.
I can't help but feel like i'm not getting it or something, but i'm less attracted to this most recent Hand Habits record than the last, though the unique lyricism still keeps my attention.
The joy punch of 80s influenced soft pop at the start of the album fades into Big Thief-ery folk that held my interest with drops of weird and small percussion.
This seriously wiggly funky groover that's oozing with jams turned me on to 70's Turkish rock and made me realize I haven't questioned leaving America on a weekly basis in 2021. RIYL Khruangbin
I did not make room for The Verve in the 90s and hearing them acoustified did not open any doors.
As if the trip hop sound of the 90s was transformed into some material that looks like transparent slime but feels like fresh air.

This was introduced to me as syrupy garbage which set a nice tone for me to listen to this a bunch, but not really pay attention, and then listen to Barbara Streisand, which seemed like old high quality syrup
A quick scan drew me in with the quality of the voice and the mellow vibes but upon further listen my 2nd impression was repeatedly confirmed - syrupy hot garbage.

If you put this on in the background to bop around to, you will miss the utter brilliance of Earl's lyrics, which are usually hidden under layers of mud, but here are at the forefront for all to behold.
With a what feels like a more glittery high quality sludge, Earl Sweatshirt makes me wish I comprehended words more cuz the moments I was able to hear them were enlightening

Things I loved about this album were OPN's production, the slow jams, and funny enough JC's job as DJ throughout the set, and though the heaters felt a bit stale, The Weeknd nevertheless added a worthy entry to his impressive resume.
My favorite part of this album is the soft rock radio station concept and I dunno, it's cool I guess, and I'm sure I'll like it more once it's tapeworm it's way into my subconscious

Aside from the simply gorgeous production on this album I have 2 theories - it's unrelatable fuckboy content with an out of place totally PG 3-song arc of 80s short film perfection beginning with Blinding Lights - OR - everything about this is 100% intentional start to finish in a nuanced character study of the complexity of what created and drives said fuckboy (broken heart, drug problem, and any number of DSM-5 diagnoses) who I still don't feel sorry for.
Cinematic, luscious, washed-out dream pop that explores unexpected (for Beach House) avenues and takes the listener on perhaps a slightly too-long journey.
I don't know what's going on, but kinda feels like a rebirth through a pink sparkly space tunnel.

reviews.text: It is a simply unbelievable album: the sound of the best band in the world taking ideas and exploring them in real time to spellbinding results.
A perfect mash-up of experimental + interpolation + pop perfection that we have come to love about Chari XCX.

CRASH immediately joins the pantheon of perfect pop albums and let me declare from the mountaintop that Crash > New Shapes > Good Ones is perhaps the greatest trio of songs to kick off a pop album EVER!!!!

A lot of people will try to pigeon-hole Nilufer by comparing her to 90s greats, but this will miss the point of just how brilliant she is on her own: this is not guitar music for the reminiscent, this is guitar music for NOW!!!
I really miss the concept of an alternative rock album and I'm thinking this might be the best alternative rock album I've heard in a long time… just go listen to it
A short EP from crooner, Orville Peck, flows nicely with his course, but still somehow smooth voice.

A little Glen Campbell mixed with Meat Loaf and a ton of fabulous sprinkles layered on top makes for an engaging listen - especially on C,mon Baby, Cry, which immediately went into my top songs of 2022 list.
I surprisingly found this scary looking country elvis shit to be catchy, clever… and even pleasent at times
I was pleasantly surprised by how dubby this was, though dubbiness and Leon's presence were an odd match in the long run.
I could go for a lot more of this sunset stroll with Leon Bridges naturally riding the laid back hooka bar vibes of Khruangbin
The nostalgic guitar lulls me in a walk meandering around a familiar yet forgotten place, finding my way home in the loveliness of Mariella.
A JAY-Z feature, Clipse reunion, and peak Pusha highlight this fun rap record that will get even the stiffest listeners bobbing their heads.
This felt like the mid 90s stopping through a stranger's spot on the way to a night at the Record Room at First Ave, the little apartment filled with smoke, beats, and rhymes from the future.
This is 100% a self-care album full of elite R&B slow jams and a few upticks in tempo to keep you from the depths of emotion that I highly recommend to anyone in need of some "me time".
Full of jams that make being broken hearted feel like a warm protective forcefield of hugs from the 80s, 90s and todays

A magical mix of everything that makes me want to dance hard with the world.

colorful energy mixed with expert songcraft and an unyielding sexual pulse makes 1999 one of the greatest albums of all time.
Despite not getting how/if the whole futuristic concept ties the album together, the sexy time vibes complimented with classic funk exceeded my expectations.

Utter brilliance as usual: funky riffs, beautiful strings, dark, poetic lyricism and a complex pallet of sounds stirred together in a way that makes you wonder if we've been following along with the greatest musicians of our time.

While it's nice to get some fresh music from the Radiohead family, I find it comforting that, despite the fact that Johnny Greenwood and Thom Yorke are the only recognizable faces and names that I associate to Radiohead, Radiohead is not Radiohead without Radiohead.
Willie can still spin a yarn and has some fun covers in this collection that as a whole sounds best when it's meditative and wise.
always nice to spend a few hours of enlightenment with willie
Nostalgic in all the signatures of his song structure and vocal lilts, modern in the content of an aging legend, with a few surprises (not Willie with a hard core metaphysical bop?!) - chef's kiss.
i can't even.
Prince and the Revolution live in their prime allows you the hear their mastery as individuals and a group in an intimate love affair to the world that is a must for any fan of Prince or live music.
What a moment in time, with Prince and his riding the line between sex and God, the Revolution in a tight perfection, and limitless joy and surprises - fucking magnificent!

reviews.text: An organic feeling tapestry with interesting lyricism and pretty arrangements make for a mood-setting listen that is more rewarding the deeper you look into it.
Pleasantly cool sunset vocally driven minimal lady folk with some fun small percussion and subtly surprising instrumental dips of which I comprehended nothing
The strength of the dreary but not hopeless songwriting had me listening for the lyrics more than
The new-and-improved Soccer Mommy: More Production! More Shoegaze! More Feels!

The album cover does a nice job of capturing the vibe cuz I found myself thinking about how satisfied I would be if I wanted to melt into a blurry pink cloud with purple vapor paisleys floating all over the place.
Not in my wheelhouse but I recognize it's good, although at it's best I just wish I were listening to Portishead.
A gentle freakiness intertwined with blazing musicianship that would have sounded 300% better if I didn't have covid.
All the things you'd expect on a veteran psych rock adventure where the clouds are the ground.
A nostalgic psychedelic trip through beaches and deserts to wind up at a soft fire by the water.

The weird pop/rock song in the middle keeps this album from being a front-to-back all-timer for me, but this super long album is mostly flush with the sort of unique, lyrically smart, engaging R&B that we've come to expect from one of the best to ever do it.

Koffee's laidback debut into the pantheon of Jamaican reggae culture is a refreshing look forward into the evolution of a genre that has travelled the world, with vision toward positivity and flat out rejection of some of the newer, unpropitious dancehall themes.
Rarely do I choose raggae, but having a voice that wants to change the world with positivity as part of my week was appreciated, and I'm happy to be on the Koffee train!

There is such a precious quality to the malaise of Yo La Tengo, and this album, which speaks to the terrible situation we humans find ourselves in, lays bare their truly unique way of writing about such painful truths in such beautiful ways.
I hope Yo La Tengo's pace of continually releasing new music that feels like a fresh perspective on the same soft noise melodic magic inspires the kids to start shoegazing right.
A masterful exercise in the melding of multiple genres that form a cohesive hour of eargasm.
perfect in every single way, laughably skillful, hooky beyond words, the best album of the year thus far by a mile.
For those of you looking for some new love making music, Kali Uchis is the latin Sade
A mostly solid album of heartache and redemption that touches my soul with each listen.
a puzzle missing four crucial pieces that you're trying to put together with your hands tied behind your back.
I can't tell if it's purely the voice or if it's the machine the propels the voice that creates a personally repellent dissonance… I think it's both… that said… 1.7 points for the moody synths
this is the soundtrack a psychadelic cocktail party that takes part in a dream inside a dream (go chicago!!)
My default frequency is joyful, soulful, multi-instrumental up-beat-driven loungy jazz… from Chicago

While I dig the beats and flows, I'm struggling to connect the shit talking to the food analogy in realization that it's probably not the point and that I'm too soft and old for a whole trap album
It breaks my heart to give this a 4, but it was only P!nk's amazing vocals that kept this marginally afloat for me.

I was pretty satisfied with the thought that maybe P!nk had pivoted to being a WWE quad threat, but I'm happy that this was better than I expected and the masses that have matured from their angst have a countryside soundtrack for stadium ribbon acrobatics.
A modern-day whizz on the harp paying tribute to Dorothy Ashby while incorporating Pete Rock and others into the mix for a soulful mix of amazing music salad!!!
The harp is a powerhouse instrument and Brandee younger leads a crew of musicians to create a balanced album that is a perfect blend of easy listening neo-soul, jazz and hip-hop.

If you aren't familiar with the human treasure Harry Belafonte, you should be… if your mental default for Day-O is B**teljuice, you should watch this live clip from Japan in 1960 to flip your setting and witness the magic

I played this album during an actual dinner party (or something close to it) and it served us well by offering smooth, beat-driven tunes flush with R&B melodies and little trinkets in the mix that were rewarding when you were able to sit back, digest, and break away from the ongoing conversation for a moment.

An instant classic: an absolutely magical explosion of uber-talented collaboration that excites the mind with brilliant, original lyricism, mind-bending beats, and a Danny Brown verse halfway through the proceedings that will absolutely stop you in your tracks.
Gently engaging dream pop with loads of fun little melodic trinkets deep in the mix that will keep you floating above water until the ride stops.
A fresh electronic take on 90s dream pop for today's robots to feel a little bit more human.
I listened to this album (which sounds like someone prompted AI to deliver 128 hours of what Metallica would sound like nowadays) so you don't have to.
If I was into masturbating to Metallica masturbating, it would've been a 10.
Interesting and unique pop songs that retain what I would describe as a nice "UK essence" and engage the listener with lyrics that are left of the dial.

album: In the End It Always Does

reviews.text: This album had me in the palm of its hand all week with its clever melodies, sleek production, and left-of-center approach to modern pop music.

For 6 minutes at a time, the sound of the Japanese House feels like my soft rock wheelhouse but my attempt to listen to it because I think I should like it made me question if I only like soft rock because the nostalgia created by it being force fed to me by the radio.

I usually try to not do research on bands and just let the music guide my review, but I read this article about Lifeguard and the fact they are teenagers from Chicago inspiring youth music communities through DIY print zines make me love their pure grungy rock even more.
The Loveliest Time is what can now be deemed as "classic" CRJ - poignant pop that doesn't take itself too seriously, yet sinks itself into the mind of the listener in uniquely addictive ways.

Let it be clear that while I don't always immediately love Carly Rae Jepsen albums, I love Carly Rae Jepsen, and I assume The Loveliest Time's disco pop will sink into my soul likely somewhere on a dance floor.
